input.quote: 2.2 Vendor will be Customer's sole and exclusive provider of hosted analytics services throughout the term.
input.rationale: Section 2.2 imposes a sole-and-exclusive supplier obligation on us (the customer) for the entire term, with no product-category limit, no 12-month cap and no automatic termination on Vendor's failure to meet service levels or delivery dates. That is exclusive dealing for the full term with no performance-based exit, i.e. walk-away territory, and it fails the fallback. It is also internally inconsistent with Section 12.3, where Vendor acknowledges that Customer has made no exclusivity or minimum-volume commitment, and there is no order-of-precedence clause to resolve the conflict. Redline deletes the exclusivity and confirms our freedom to source from third parties, aligning Section 2.2 with Section 12.3; if Vendor pushes back, the fallback (a single defined product category, 12 months, terminating automatically on any SLA or delivery failure) would be the limit of what we can accept.

ops.oldText: 2.2 Vendor will be Customer's sole and exclusive provider of hosted analytics services throughout the term.
ops.newText: 2.2 Vendor will be a provider of hosted analytics services to Customer. Customer is under no obligation to purchase any minimum volume of services from Vendor and remains free to obtain analytics or other services from any third party at any time.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We have removed the sole-and-exclusive supplier commitment in Section 2.2: our playbook does not permit exclusivity obligations on the customer, and this one would run for the full term with no performance-based exit. It also directly contradicts Section 12.3, in which Vendor acknowledges that we have made no exclusivity or minimum-volume commitment.
proposal.summary: Remove Customer exclusivity in § 2.2 and confirm freedom to use other suppliers.
